A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMCR benchmark and experiments. Text, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally includes Appendix A-C and supplementary figures.

before.justification: Table 3 reports original evaluations of 18 VLMs. Figures 3-7 report circular-evaluation, resolution, CoT and error analyses.

after.justification: The original model evaluations and analyses remain, supplemented by worked GPT-4o error cases in Figures S.22-S.28.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and evaluation procedures remain unchanged, including expert annotation, LLM-assisted filtering and cross-checking. The appendix documents existing prompting and extraction procedures without establishing a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use 31 papers, 276 questions, seven AI subjects and ten question categories. The appendix illustrates existing benchmark coverage rather than adding datasets, domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same 15 open-source and three proprietary models, and the existing analyses retain their comparator sets. Figure S.10 visualizes a subset of previously reported models; models appearing inside source-paper examples are not additional MMCR evaluations.

E3.justification: Both retain 144-DPI page rendering, the same image-input handling, five answer-option rotations and exact-match scoring. The resolution and CoT comparisons are unchanged. Appendix B newly discloses prompts and extraction details without reporting revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Figures S.22-S.28 add worked examples for all seven existing error categories, extending v1's distribution and single perceptual-error example. This elaborates the same 109-error audit; the circular-evaluation, resolution and CoT analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The unchanged five-option circular evaluation is an evaluation procedure, not newly added uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes InternVL2.5-8B's text-comprehension accuracy from 4.84% to 31.43%, consistent with its unchanged 12.32% overall score. Other aggregate results remain unchanged. The appendix adds case-level responses, while its distribution and radar charts redisplay existing results.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are added or revised. Appendix A's multi-hop explanation is conceptual; equations and pseudocode reproduced in benchmark examples are source material rather than new theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and principal claims about cross-source difficulty, model performance and scale-dependent CoT effects. The appendix elaborates their support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The appendix adds a bridge-entity explanation of reasoning and attributes strong text comprehension partly to extensive pretraining. V2 removes the explicit limitation linking annotation costs to the benchmark's restricted scale, together with the proposed volunteer-annotation platform.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies exact CoT and non-CoT prompts and explains option-identifier matching, fallback answer-text matching and extraction failure. Appendix C documents annotator training, domain allocation, review and remediation. These substantial reproducibility disclosures were only summarized or referred to unavailable supplementary material in v1.

R1.justification: The 38-entry bibliography and main related-work discussion remain unchanged. Appendix A adds an explicit comparison with HotpotQA's bridge-entity and multi-hop reasoning, modestly extending MMCR's research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands the exposition through a structured Appendix A-C covering reasoning, evaluation, annotation and error mechanisms. The main prose and section order are largely retained, with smaller affiliation edits, added acknowledgements and removal of the limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures S.8-S.28 and Table S.4, including distribution charts, radar plots, prompt panels, annotation guidance and extensive illustrated examples. Some displays repackage existing statistics; others add source-linked demonstrations and error cases. Main-text displays are retained with modest layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The appendix makes the existing evaluation easier to reproduce and inspect through explicit prompts, extraction rules and worked examples, while Table 3 corrects a score. These benefits outweigh limited drawbacks, including removal of the explicit benchmark-scale limitation and editing errors such as Figure S.23's unrelated question paired with training-time answer options.
